title: The Wildcat guide to well-being, sexual health resources on campus
text:
Staying healthy in college is about far more than working out regularly at the gym or hitting your daily protein intake with a peanut butter shake from Shake Smart.
One of the biggest misconceptions in health is that everyone else already knows what they’re doing. The truth is that every student, whether it’s their first week on campus or senior year, needs support sometimes. Knowing where to turn when you need support is just as important as knowing where your classes are.
Northwestern offers a wide range of offices and programs to support students’ emotional, sexual and spiritual well-being. Beyond leaning on new friends, grabbing a chocolate fudge brownie from Sargent Dining Commons or taking a headphones-on walk around the Lakefill, here’s a list of campus resources to help you navigate relationships, pleasure, sexuality, consent and all the other firsts that come with college.
Center for Student Advocacy and Wellness
If you only remember one office from the True Northwestern Dialogues series during Wildcat Welcome, make it CSAW. Located on the third floor of Searle Hall, CSAW offers confidential support for everything from sexual health questions to relationship concerns, wellness coaching to survivor advocacy. You can also pick up free safe sex supplies, meet one-on-one with a sexual health expert and attend programs like Sexy Munchies and bingo. CSAW also hosts Red Watch Band and bystander intervention training.
Gender and Sexuality Resource Center
Need a cozy study spot? Looking for community? Or just hoping to score a free snack between classes? GSRC, tucked inside Foster-Walker House 5, offers all three. The center supports LGBTQIA+ students and allies through community events, educational programs and visibility initiatives throughout the academic year. GSRC’s newsletter shares events from craft nights to community conversations. The snacks live up to the hype, but most students stay for the people.
Northwestern Medicine Student Health Service
Located in Searle Hall, NU Health Services is the place to go for routine medical care, including STI testing, pregnancy testing, contraception and other sexual and reproductive health services. Appointments can be made through MyNM, so creating an account before you need it can save time later.
Sexual Health and Assault Peer Educators
Sometimes the easiest person to talk to is another student. SHAPE is a student-led education group that leads workshops and campus conversations about consent, healthy relationships, sexual health and assault prevention. The chapter also organizes NU’s annual Sex Week, bringing together workshops, community discussions and other events on topics related to sexual health and wellness. If you end up enjoying the programming, applications to become a peer educator open each fall.
Masculinity, Allyship, Reflection and Solidarity
MARS is an all-male peer education group that encourages conversations about healthy masculinity, allyship and preventing sexual violence. Through workshops and peer discussions, members challenge stereotypes, promote healthy relationships and work to combat rape culture on campus.
Student Enrichment Services
Located in Foster-Walker House 6, SES supports first-generation and lower-income students through mentoring, community-building and practical resources that make college more accessible. If you qualify, the SES One Form connects students with funding for everything from winter coats and professional clothing to club expenses and emergency needs. It is one of those resources upperclassmen wish they had started using sooner.
